title: Health Canada issues warning on rare risk of vision loss with semaglutide GLP-1 drugs
summary: A safety review from Health Canada has found a possible link between semaglutide GLP-1 drugs and a rare form of vision loss.

image.caption: Health Canada has issued a public warning about the 'very rare but serious' risk of vision loss tied to semaglutide GLP-1 drugs. (CBC)

blocks.text: A safety review from Health Canada has found a possible link between semaglutide GLP-1 drugs and a rare form of vision loss.
Federal team's safety review found possible link between use of drugs and 'very rare' eye condition
Health Canada has issued a public warning about the "very rare but serious" risk of vision loss tied to semaglutide GLP-1 drugs, known by brand names such as Ozempic, Rybelsus, and Wegovy.

On the heels of similar warnings in the U.S. and Europe, the federal department announced on Wednesday that it had completed its own safety review which found a possible link between prescription semaglutide drugs and the risk of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).
Described by Health Canada as "very rare," the eye condition causes sudden, painless blindness or vision changes due to reduced blood flow to the optic nerve.
The condition has no known treatment.
